author: Brenton Kemp
title: Gregory Santos declares free agency
desc: Reliever Gregory Santos has cleared waivers and has declared free agency in lieu of an outright assignment to the minors.
impact: The Giants outrighted Santos to Triple-A Sacramento after designating him for assignment, but the 26-year-old has instead chosen to become a free agent. Santos appeared in just three games for the Giants this season and owns a respectable 4.14 ERA across 84 MLB appearances, a figure that should generate some interest on the open market.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Tim Elko (knee) beginning rehab assignment Wednesday
desc: White Sox first baseman Tim Elko is beginning a minor league rehab assignment with High-A Winston-Salem on Wednesday.
impact: Elko underwent ACL surgery on his right knee in October, but despite limited information on his recovery, he will begin a rehab assignment in the low minors on Wednesday. He is listed with a July timetable to return, although he will need notable time in the minors before re-entering the lineup for the first-place White Sox.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Matt Bowman signs minors deal with Twins
desc: The Twins have signed right-hander Matt Bowman to a minor-league deal.
impact: Bowman recently opted out of his contract with the Blue Jays and became a free agent. Bowman is expected to join the bullpen of Triple-A St. Paul, where he began the season, posting a 1.69 ERA in 14 appearances (two starts).

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Justin Verlander to retire after 2026 season
desc: Tigers right-hander Justin Verlander announced that he will retire following the 2026 season.
impact: On the same day he was named to the American League All-Star roster as a Legeng Pick, Verlander was quick to announce that the time has come to call it career after this season. The future first-ballot Hall of Famer has made just one start for the Tigers this season due to hip and hamstring injuries, but will technically retire as a 10-time All-Star with a Rookie of the Year, MVP, three AL Cy Young Awards, and two World Series championships under his belt. Fittingly, he will retire with the Tigers, who drafted him second overall in 2004.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Tyler Soderstrom (hip) could return Wednesday
desc: Athletics outfielder Tyler Soderstrom (hip) could be activated as soon as Wednesday versus the Tigers.
impact: Soderstrom has been sidelined with left hip soreness since June 29, but has participated in defense, hitting, and running drills of late. It appears he could return for either Wednesday's or Thursday's game against the Tigers.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Jeremy Pena (calf) expected to return Friday
desc: Astros shortstop Jeremy Pena (calf) is expected to return to the lineup on Friday against the Rangers.
impact: Pena appeared for Triple-A Sugar Land in a rehab game on Tuesday, and went 1-for-4 with an RBI double. The 28-year-old has had trouble staying healthy this season, but has been productive when on the field, hitting .295 with six homers, eight stolen bases, and a .799 OPS across 48 games.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Ronel Blanco (elbow) throws 36 pitches in rehab outing Tuesday
desc: Astros right-hander Ronel Blanco pitched two scoreless innings on 36 pitches for Triple-A Sugar Land on Tuesday.
impact: While only half of his 36 pitches went for strikes, Blanco managed to pitch a pair of scoreless frames before the game was called due to weather. Blanco, who could return to the Astros' rotation once healthy, has been sidelined since undergoing Tommy John surgery after nine starts in 2025 and is expected to return in late July, although early August could also be a possibility depending on his build-up.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Lance McCullers (shoulder) throws 77 pitches in rehab outing Tuesday
desc: Astros right-hander Lance McCullers Jr. (shoulder) threw four innings and 77 pitches for Triple-A Sugar Land on Tuesday.
impact: McCullers allowed four runs (two earned) on three hits and three walks in the outing. While not the result the Astros would hope for, the main focus is the build-up to 77 pitches in what marked McCullers' third rehab start in his recovery from a right rotator cuff impingement. The oft-injured veteran is expected to return at some point in July.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Jordan Montgomery (elbow) sharp in rehab start Tuesday
desc: Rangers left-hander Jordan Montgomery (elbow) pitched three scoreless innings in a rehab start for Triple-A Round Rock on Tuesday.
impact: Montgomery scattered five hits in the outing, but did not walk a batter while striking out three. The left-hander hasn't appeared on a big-league mound since September 22, 2024 while with the D-backs due to a left UCL surgery. The Rangers are hoping the veteran can return shortly after the All-Star break.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Ceddanne Rafaela goes deep in win over White Sox
desc: Ceddanne Rafaela went 2-for-5 in Tuesday's 8-1 win over the White Sox with a home run, one run scored, and two RBI.
impact: Rafaela continues a productive stretch at the plate, picking up hits in 10 of his last 13 contests. The outfielder offers manager Chad Tracy one of the more reliable bats in an inconsistent Red Sox lineup, batting .284 with eight homers, 38 RBI, 39 runs scored, and 12 stolen bases across 85 games.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Jacob deGrom (hip/leg) expects to make next start
desc: Rangers right-hander Jacob deGrom (hip/leg) expects to make his next start after leaving Tuesday's game against the Angels after five innings.
impact: deGrom allowed two runs across five innings before leaving after throwing 80 pitches with left hip/leg soreness on Tuesday. The veteran did not sound overly concerned postgame and expects to make his next turn through the rotation, which is scheduled for Sunday at home against the rival Astros.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Andruw Monasterio homers, steals base in win over White Sox
desc: Andruw Monasterio went 2-for-4 in Tuesday's win over the White Sox with a solo home run, one walk, and one stolen base.
impact: Monasterio has heated up at the plate of late, recording hits in each of his last four contests. The infielder has fought issues with consistency at the plate for much of the season however, batting .228 with four homers, 13 RBI, 17 runs scored, and two stolen bases across 54 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Payton Tolle cruises through six in win over White Sox
desc: Payton Tolle allowed two hits and one walk while striking out six over six scoreless innings in Tuesday's win over the White Sox.
impact: Tolle has struggled to miss opposing bats of late, allowing three earned runs or more in four of his last six contests. The left-hander remains one of many arms in the Red Sox rotation that have fallen victim to inconsistent support from an underperforming lineup to this point, carrying a 3.14 ERA and 1.07 WHIP to go with a 5-6 record and 9.0 K/9 ratio across 14 starts.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Mike Trout (hamstring) on track to return Wednesday
desc: Angels outfielder Mike Trout (hamstring) is on track to return from the injured list on Wednesday against the Rangers.
impact: Trout, out since June 18 with a right hamstring strain, ran the bases with no issues and performed a full pregame routine prior to Tuesday's game against the Rangers. Afterward, Angels skipper Kurt Suzuki said things are "definitely looking good", and if Trout feel ready to go on Wednesday, he will likely be back in the starting lineup. The future Hall of Famer has hit .234 with 17 home runs, 54 runs, 36 RBI, seven stolen bases, and an .866 OPS across 74 games this season.
